top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a datable invention, Katori's magic-wavelength lattice and its realisation by Ye at the 10^-18 level, with a stable interpretation, reproduction with Sr, Yb and Hg in many laboratories, uses already delivered in tests of constants, new-physics searches and relativistic geodesy, and a two-name allocation that follows the concept and its decisive realisation. A citation confined to the lattice architecture does not overlap the 2005 comb or 2012 single-ion prizes. I rank P002 second because its Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio is coherent and settled, but it leaves out the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that directed the HgTe experiment, and P003 third because the pairing mechanism and disorder sensitivity are not yet settled; both still rank above no award.
recusal_note: No connection to Katori, Ye or the other proposed laureates is documented in my profile. My field of atomic theory is close to the clock subject, and I have collaborated with groups in attosecond and ion-storage physics, but none of the named laureates is among them.
